title: Arshdeep Singh Retires Hurt With Arm Blow as West Indies Level Series in Hyderabad
excerpt: A Joseph short ball struck the left-arm pacer in the final over of the fourth T20I; the BCCI has given no medical update, with the series decider in Bengaluru on October 17 and a New Zealand series to follow.
body:
• Arshdeep Singh retired hurt on 5 off 4 balls in the final over of India's chase in Hyderabad, after a Shamar Joseph short ball struck his left arm and shoulder area; captain Shreyas Iyer called the innings off.
  • West Indies won the fourth T20I by 24 runs — 247/3 against India's 223 — behind Shai Hope's 102 off 50 balls and Keemo Paul's five-wicket haul, levelling the series 2-2.
  • The BCCI has issued no official medical update, and reports differ on whether the blow landed on the shoulder or the left bicep; scans have been reported as likely.
  • The series decider is on Saturday, October 17 at Bengaluru's M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, with a five-match T20I series against New Zealand to follow — Arshdeep's new-ball role makes his fitness a selection issue for both.

India's defeat in the fourth T20I against the West Indies ended with a sight their management did not want: Arshdeep Singh on the ground in the final over, struck by a Shamar Joseph short ball, and then walking off retired hurt as captain Shreyas Iyer declared the innings closed. West Indies won by 24 runs at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad to level the five-match series 2-2, but the fitness of India's senior left-arm quick now leads the agenda before Saturday's decider in Bengaluru.

How the Injury Happened

Arshdeep came in at the fall of the ninth wicket with the chase effectively gone — India needed about 30 from the final over. Joseph went short; Arshdeep backed away to pull and the ball thudded into his left bicep and shoulder area. He stayed down in clear discomfort while the physio and support staff came out twice. After discussion with umpire Nitin Menon, and with Iyer signalling from the dugout, Arshdeep retired hurt on 5 off 4 balls, ending India's innings at 223 in 19.4 overs, according to SportsTiger's ball-by-ball account.

Joseph's repeated short-pitched attack on a tail-ender in a decided game drew criticism. Former Bengal cricketer Shreevats Goswami called the approach unsportsmanlike, arguing a conventional line would have closed the match without targeting a number eleven who could not win it.

The Match It Ended

West Indies' total was built on a commanding hundred from Shai Hope, who reached his century with successive sixes off the final deliveries of the innings as the visitors posted 247/3. India's reply started at a sprint — Sanju Samson smashed 56 off 23 balls and Tilak Varma made 43 off 25 — but Keemo Paul's five-wicket haul kept breaking partnerships, and the required rate outran the chase. Arshdeep had a hard night with the ball before his injury, conceding 52 runs and dismissing Rovman Powell for 24; Mayank Yadav also went for 52 in an innings containing 17 sixes.

What Is Known About the Injury

Very little, officially. The BCCI has released no medical bulletin. Reports describe the injury variously as a shoulder knock and a blow to the left bicep — for a left-arm bowler, both descriptions point at the same bowling arm, which is why the concern is real rather than routine. Cricket News reported that scans may be needed and that team management is yet to confirm anything; ESPNcricinfo's live coverage recorded Arshdeep clutching his left shoulder as he left the field. Iyer's decision to end the innings rather than send out the last batter underlined the priority: protect the bowler, not the scoreline.

Why the Timing Is Awkward

India have two days before the decider at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium on October 17, and a five-match T20I series against New Zealand follows on the schedule. Arshdeep has been selected for the New Zealand series, and his value is structural: he is India's first-choice new-ball and death-overs left-armer, a role no like-for-like replacement in the current squad fills. A bruised arm that settles in 48 hours is an anecdote; anything involving the shoulder joint becomes a series-level problem. Expect an update only after assessment — and expect India to wrap their most important white-ball seamer in cotton wool until they get one.
